section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the concepts of "this night" and "that night" in terms of faith versus perception, and how toil in Torah and livelihood brings one to the level of "this night."
section.t: [And to note,
that in the above discourses the concept of "this night" and "that night" is explained in a different manner.
For the concept of "day" is that there is a vision of G-dliness, or at least a comprehension of G-dliness32,
but when there is only faith, it is called by the name "night."
And the concept of "this night" is that the faith is with great intensity and with ultimate certainty,
in the manner of the certainty of vision.
And this is what is written33
"A night of watchings... it is this night,"
that the revelation that was then
(this)
was not in a manner that the darkness of night was nullified,
for they were still in exile34,
but rather their faith at that time was with absolute certainty,
like the certainty of vision.
[And it is explained there,
that their reaching the level of "this night" came about through their labor in Egypt with mortar and bricks.
And likewise now,
in order that there be "this night,"
that even during the time of exile there should be this level,
it is through toil and exertion in the study of Torah,
"mortar" refers to a fortiori reasoning and "bricks" refers to clarifying the halachah35,
and likewise through toil and exertion in the troubles of earning a livelihood, "by the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread"36,
and like "this night" of the Exodus from Egypt, which they attained through their labor with mortar and bricks,
mortar and bricks in their literal sense.
And this is what they said37
"Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah, they remove from him the yoke of worldly occupation"38
"and whoever casts off from himself the yoke of Torah, they place upon him the yoke of worldly occupation,"
for even through the yoke of worldly occupation one reaches the level of "this night"].
And according to this explanation
(in the discourses)
of "this night,"
it must be said,
that "that night" is when even the certainty of faith is lacking.
And there is yet another explanation of "this night" and "that night,"
that the words "this" and "that" refer to the night.
Whether the night is revealed
(this)
so that it is felt that it is night,
or whether the night is hidden
(that)
so that it is not felt that it is night].

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the two aspects of Ein Sof—"above above" and "below below"—and how they correspond to the roots of day, "that day," "this day," and night.
section.t: And this will be understood according to what is explained in many places39
in the explanation of the statement40
"Ein Sof is above above, without end, and below below, without limit,"
that "below below etc." is the aspect of the spreading forth and revelation of Ein Sof,
that it spreads forth and is revealed down to below below,
and "above above etc." is the aspect of the concealment and elevation within Ein Sof,
that it is elevated and concealed in concealment after concealment and in elevation after elevation,
above above.
And behold, even the concept of "below below etc." as it is in Ein Sof is a level of concealment.
For the entirety of the light before the tzimtzum is light included in His Essence41,
and light included in the Luminary is above revelation42.
And that it spreads forth and is revealed down to below below,
behold, the revelation drawn from it after the tzimtzum
(the light of the line,
and even the encompassing light)
is only an illumination from the light before the tzimtzum.
But nevertheless,
since that Ein Sof is "below below etc." is the power of spreading forth and revelation of Ein Sof,
behold, even as it is in its source,
it is the aspect of revelation.
And as explained in the continuation of the discourse of Hilula43,
that in His very Essence it is in a state of revelation.
But not so that Ein Sof is "above above etc.," which is that even in His Essence it is not in the category of revelation.
And it may be said,
that the root of the two concepts of day,
"that day" and "this day,"
is in the concept of "below below etc."
That the actual revelation
(after the tzimtzum)
is the root of "this day,"
and the power of revelation of Ein Sof
(before the tzimtzum)
is the root of "that day."
And the root of night
(which is above even "that day")
is in the concept of "above above etc."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that there are two aspects within the power of concealment of Ein Sof, which are the source for two purposes of tzimtzum: one for the sake of revelation, and the other to reveal the power of concealment itself.
section.t: And behold, it is known that in tzimtzum there are two aspects.
That the tzimtzum is for the sake of revelation
[and within this itself there are two aspects.
That specifically through the tzimtzum there will be in the future the revelation of Ein Sof even in the worlds,
and that through the tzimtzum there will be the revelation of the inwardness and essence of Ein Sof, which is above even the light that shone before the tzimtzum]44,
and that in the tzimtzum itself is revealed the perfection of Ein Sof, that it is not, Heaven forbid, limited to the aspect of revelation, and it also has the power of concealment.
And it may be said,
that that there are two aspects in tzimtzum,
is,
because in the power of concealment of Ein Sof,
the root of tzimtzum,
there are two levels.
The power of concealment as it relates to the matter of revelation
[that even this level in the power of concealment of Ein Sof is above the power of revelation,
but nevertheless, it is connected to revelation],
for the tzimtzum drawn from this level is for the sake of revelation.
And the very essence of the power of concealment
(which is above revelation),
for the tzimtzum drawn from this level is
(not for the sake of revelation,
but rather)
that in the tzimtzum itself is revealed the power of concealment.
